chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever is lazy regarding his purification and his prayer, there is no goodness in him for the matter of his Hereafter, and whoever is lazy regarding that which rectifies the matter of his livelihood, there is no goodness in him for the matter of his world.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of laziness in prayer and livelihood according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a holistic view of faith where spiritual negligence (tahur and salah) and worldly negligence (kasal over livelihood) are both detrimental, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing 'ibadat and mu'amalat. It underscores that true piety requires diligence in both the religious and material spheres, as neglect in either domain compromises one's overall spiritual and temporal well-being.
